title: Hot alkaline lysis gDNA extraction from formalin-fixed archival tissues
author: Erin E Hahn

steps.title: Measure media pH
steps.instruction: Using an Orion Versa Star Pro benchtop pH meter (Thermo Scientific) or an equivalent meter suitable for ethanol‑containing media, measure the pH of the specimen media.

steps.title: Visually assess specimen safety
steps.instruction: Inspect the specimen; if it appears decomposed, lacks internal organs, or shows signs of prior organ removal, consider an alternative specimen. Treat all media as if it contains formaldehyde and wear appropriate PPE following your facility’s Safe Work Instructions.

steps.title: Aliquot media for testing
steps.instruction: Transfer at least 7 mL of the specimen media from the jar into a 15 mL tube so the pH probe can be fully immersed.

steps.title: Measure residual formaldehyde
steps.instruction: Use MQuant test strips (Merck) to determine formaldehyde concentration; if the concentration exceeds the strip’s upper detection limit, dilute the media 1:10 with ultra‑pure water and repeat the test.

steps.title: Rate specimen suitability
steps.instruction: If pH < 6 or formaldehyde > 10 000 mg/L, select another specimen or limit analysis to small amplicons. If pH is neutral and formaldehyde is between 0 and 10 000 mg/L, treat as well‑preserved formalin‑fixed tissue. If pH is neutral and no formaldehyde is detectable, treat as ethanol‑preserved.

steps.title: Prepare chilled reagents
steps.instruction: Chill the following reagents to 4 °C: 50 % ethanol, 30 % ethanol, MilliQ water, and Glycine‑Tris‑EDTA buffer (GTE: 100 mM glycine, 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA).

steps.title: Dissect tissue into ethanol
steps.instruction: Excise at least 50 mg of target tissue and place it in a 2 mL tube containing 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Weigh and record tissue mass
steps.instruction: Weigh the tissue; if more than 50 mg is available, subsample to 50 mg for optimal pulverisation (larger amounts are permissible).

steps.title: Load tissue into Covaris bag
steps.instruction: Transfer the tissue to an extra‑thick TT05 (or TT1) Covaris tissueTUBE bag, attach a 1 mL Covaris milliTUBE to seal the bag, and secure the assembly with the appropriate holder or plug.

substeps.instruction: Use extra‑thick TT05 or TT1 bags; the milliTUBE serves as a seal and handling point.
If using a TT1, attach an adapter; alternatively, use a tissueTUBE plug and holder.

steps.title: Flash‑freeze tissue bag
steps.instruction: Dispense ~1 L liquid nitrogen into a cryo‑dewar, immerse the tissueTUBE bag for ~30 seconds, wearing cryogenic PPE and following facility safety procedures.

steps.title: Apply CryoPrep impacts
steps.instruction: Using the Covaris CryoPrep, deliver 2–3 level‑6 impacts, flash‑freezing the sample between impacts; stop if the bag shows loss of integrity. The tissue should appear flattened, not a fine powder.

steps.title: Resuspend in 50 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Resuspend the frozen tissue in cold 50 % ethanol, transfer to a 15 mL tube with a wide‑bore tip, rinse the bag with additional cold 50 % ethanol, bring the total volume to 10 mL, and rock for 10 min at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Transfer to 15 mL tube; rinse bag with cold 50 % ethanol.
Adjust volume to 10 mL with cold 50 % ethanol.

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend in 30 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Spin the tube 10 min at 750 × g, 4 °C; discard supernatant, add 10 mL cold 30 % ethanol, and rock for 10 min at 4 °C. Increase g‑force if the pellet does not form adequately.

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend in MilliQ water
steps.instruction: Spin 10 min at 750 × g, 4 °C; discard supernatant, add 10 mL cold MilliQ water, and rock for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend in GTE buffer
steps.instruction: Spin 10 min at 750 × g, 4 °C; discard supernatant, add 10 mL cold GTE buffer, and rock overnight (≈16 h) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Reduce GTE volume to 1 mL
steps.instruction: On Day 2, spin the tube 10 min at 750 × g, 4 °C and remove all but 1 mL of the GTE buffer.

steps.title: Transfer tissue to screw‑cap tube
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in the remaining 1 mL GTE and transfer the suspension to a 2 mL screw‑cap tube using a wide‑bore tip.

steps.title: Add alkaline lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Spin the screw‑cap tube 10 min at 750 × g, 4 °C; discard supernatant and add 500 µL alkaline lysis buffer (0.1 M NaOH, pH 13; 1 % SDS). Consult the SDS and NaOH safety data sheets.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL alkaline lysis buffer (0.1 M NaOH, pH 13; 1 % SDS).

steps.title: Autoclave for alkaline lysis
steps.instruction: Place the tube upright in an autoclave‑safe container (e.g., tip box propped with aluminium foil) and autoclave at 120 °C for a total of 25 minutes (multiple shorter cycles are acceptable). The lysate should become clear to dark red‑brown with no visible tissue chunks.

steps.title: First phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1) to the lysate, vortex briefly, and rock for 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Separate aqueous phase (first)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at maximum microcentrifuge speed for 5 min at room temperature; transfer the aqueous phase to a new 2 mL tube, then add 100 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 to the remaining organic phase and rock 5 min.

substeps.instruction: Move aqueous phase to new tube.
Add 100 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 to organic phase.

steps.title: Combine aqueous phases
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the organic‑phase tube again at maximum speed for 5 min at room temperature, then combine its aqueous phase with the first aqueous extract; discard all organic phases according to waste protocols.

steps.title: Optional RNase treatment
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL RNase A to the combined aqueous extract and incubate 30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Repeat phenol‑chloroform extractions
steps.instruction: Perform additional phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol extractions (equal volume) until the aqueous phase is clear; if the phase is cloudy, add 200 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 before re‑extracting. Typically repeat 1–2 times.

steps.title: Chloroform wash
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of chloroform to the cleared aqueous extract, rock 5 min at room temperature, then centrifuge at maximum speed for 5 min at room temperature and transfer the aqueous phase to a new tube.

steps.title: Repeat chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Repeat the chloroform extraction until no phenol remains (usually a single repeat is sufficient).

steps.title: Bind DNA to magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Add 1.5× the volume of a small‑fragment‑optimised magnetic bead solution to the aqueous DNA solution and incubate 15 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Magnetically separate beads
steps.instruction: Briefly spin the tubes, place them on a magnetic rack for 10 min or until the solution is clear.

steps.title: Wash bead pellet
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and wash the bead pellet twice with fresh 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Dry beads
steps.instruction: Briefly spin, return tubes to the magnet, remove residual ethanol with a small‑volume pipette, and air‑dry the beads for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, pipette up and down to resuspend the beads, incubate 15 min at 37 °C, then place on the magnet for 15 min to pellet the beads.

steps.title: Collect purified DNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant containing the purified DNA to a new tube.

steps.title: Quantify DNA and assess fragment size
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with a Qubit dsDNA HS kit and evaluate fragment size distribution on a Tapestation High Sensitivity D1000 chip; samples yielding ≥200 ng DNA per 50 mg tissue and mean fragment size >150 bp are considered suitable for sequencing.

steps.title: Store dissected tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer the dissected tissue (post‑extraction) to room temperature storage until further processing.
